science.title: Mars Curiosity Rover Discovers Massive Field of Polygons
science.description: The surface of Mars is home to some of the most breathtaking and awe-inspiring landscapes in the solar system. This is primarily due to the Red Planet lacking several re-surfacing processes that Earth possesses, including plate tectonics, volcanism, and flowing water. While Mars does have dust storms, this has done little to reshape the planet’s surface, which has remained largely undisturbed for billions of years. However, this near-pristine landscape has enabled scientists to look back in time while slowly piecing together what Mars was like long ago.

science.title: Molecular memory: How a mother's age echoes in her offspring's cells
science.description: In humans and many other animals, a mother's age can affect the physical and behavioral characteristics of the next generation. Scientists call these changes maternal age effects, and while they are widespread across the animal kingdom, researchers still don't fully understand how or why they occur.

science.title: MOTHRA Shows Us A Star Being Recycled in the Helix Nebula
science.description: Astronomers used new MOTHRA telescope in Chile to image the famous Helix Nebula. They found 22 glowing shock waves where stellar debris from a dying star collided with interstellar gas. After colliding with gas, stellar fragments remain intact for just 10,000 years, the team estimates. The observations show how dying stars are recycled and return material to the interstellar medium to form new stars and planets.

science.title: Subtype-specific heterogeneity of anti-epidermal growth factor receptor antibody sensitivity in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer revealed by patient-derived organoids
science.description: Anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (anti-EGFR) antibodies are widely used in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC), and KRAS mutation status is commonly used as a predictive biomarker for therapeutic responsiveness. Nevertheless, emerging evidence suggests that drug sensitivity among KRAS-mutant CRC is heterogeneous and varies according to mutation subtype. In this study, we reevaluated the determinants of anti-EGFR antibody sensitivity using a patient-derived CRC organoid library. Eight organoid lines comprising KRAS wild-type, KRAS G12-mutant, and KRAS G13-mutant tumors were subjected to drug sensitivity assays. Although KRAS G12-mutant organoids generally exhibited reduced responsiveness to anti-EGFR antibodies, KRAS G13-mutant organoids demonstrated sensitivity comparable to that of KRAS wild-type organoids. Transcriptomic analysis of a KRAS G13-mutant organoid after anti-EGFR antibody treatment revealed significant alterations in gene expression, with enrichment of MYC-related signaling pathways. These results were supported by in silico analyses using public cancer cell line datasets, which showed relatively lower IC50 values for KRAS G13-mutant cells than for KRAS G12-mutant cells. Moreover, anti-EGFR antibody treatment induced the expression of apoptosis-related genes in KRAS G13-mutant organoids, and pharmacological inhibition of MYC signaling partially attenuated drug sensitivity, indicating a functional role for MYC activation in mediating therapeutic response. Altogether, our results demonstrate heterogeneity in anti-EGFR antibody sensitivity among KRAS-mutant CRCs and identify KRAS G13-mutant tumors as a subset with preserved responsiveness. These data provide mechanistic insights into subtype-specific differences in therapeutic vulnerability and suggest that downstream transcriptional programs, including MYC signaling, contribute to sensitivity to EGFR-targeted therapy.

science.title: Hybrid nanowire metamaterials with ultra-wideband epsilon-near-zero mode tuning for nanophotonic applications
science.description: This work investigates the linear and nonlinear optical properties and guided wave modes of hybrid nanowire metamaterials (HNW-MMs), focusing on controlling their transmission characteristics. The epsilon-near-zero and hyperbolic responses of such structures are analyzed using effective medium theory, dispersion relations, and the FDTD method, under irradiation with transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) beams. Our study reveals that including silicon cores within the nanowires significantly enhances the tunability of the optical response of the metamaterial, with the emergence of additional modes at higher wavelengths. Unlike conventional nanowire MMs, these hybrid structures exhibit extra guided modes that are unique to their configuration and physical structure. The results demonstrate that by adjusting the filling ratios, the new modes can be fully controlled from the visible to the infrared (IR) range. In specific configurations, one of the new modes can achieve epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) characteristics. This work introduces a novel platform that combines controllable modes with ENZ behavior, enabling advanced functionalities not achievable in traditional metamaterial designs. Using this tunability and ENZ properties as a novel approach, a band-stop adjustable optical filter within the ENZ bandwidth is designed and simulated. Furthermore, the Kerr nonlinear effect in ENZ mode is investigated, and highly efficient all-optical nonlinear switches and relays at the nanoscale are presented.

science.title: Analytical study of dual-material gate inverted T-TFET biosensor for ultra-sensitive detection
science.description: Tunnel field effect transistors (TFETs) have shown significant promise in the context of analog and mixed-signal circuit applications because of their high on-state current, low off-state leakage. As devices are being scaled down further in dimensions, conventional devices face severe short-channel effects (SCE), which have a detrimental impact on device characteristics. To overcome these issues, a variety of novel devices have been explored in recent years. Among these devices, the Dual Metal Gate T-shaped TFET biosensor device has shown promise in terms of electrostatic control and SCE suppression. An analytical model of a Dual Metal Gate T-shaped TFET biosensor device has been proposed in the present work with the aim of investigating the characteristics of the device. To obtain an analytical expression of the surface potential, threshold voltage, electric field, and sensitivity and drain current of the device, the two-dimensional Poisson equation has been solved with suitable boundary conditions using a parabolic potential approximation. The inverted T-shape of the TFET device ensures low power operation and high sensitivity in the subthreshold regime. Also, the device exhibits the ability of biosensing without the need for labeling.

science.title: Deep adaptive cryptographic video watermarking using hybrid DCT-SVD and CNN-based adaptive embedding
science.description: As the use of digital multimedia distribution, which includes cloud service providers, social networks and streaming services, has grown rapidly, there has been increasing demand for robustly protecting copyright, verifying content authenticity and determining ownership. Previous watermarking methods may be difficult to balance the watermarking goals—imperceptibility, robustness, and security, and traditional cryptographic approaches can provide security during the transmission but they cannot support the ownership information after de-cryption. To address these issues, the Deep Adaptive Cryptographic Video Watermarking Framework is proposed in this paper, which combines the transform domain based watermark embedding technique with adaptive embedding approach based on deep learning and chaotic encryption. The framework makes use of the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) together with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) for embedding the encrypted watermark information into the mid frequency coefficient, the strength of embedding information is predicted adaptively based on the local spatial-frequency characteristics, and a light-convolutional network is used for the prediction. A noisy channel model for the residual neural decoder recovers the embedded watermark from corrupted video frames to be more resilient for compression, Gaussian noise, cropping, scaling and frame manipulation events. Choa’s chaotic key-generation mechanism is used in a secure hash-assisted way, which is used independently to generate keys for preventing the tampering of image watermark using the neural network. By simulation testing of the system under various attacking conditions, (both signal processing and geometric attacks), the system is evaluated to show that the proposed framework meets high visual qualities and the watermark can be recovered under different attacks and various watermark payloads. The results also show the well-known trade-off between watermark capacity and its imperceptibility and extraction accuracy, and a higher payload results in a moderate decrease of the PSNR and consequently, an increase of the BER in the case of severe attacks. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed framework offers a well-balanced performance among the visual quality, robustness, and payload security as compared with the conventional transform-domain and existing watermarking approaches using deep learning. All of the above makes the proposed scheme can be used as a means of secure authentication for multimedia, copyright protection and protected video distribution.
